correctness.rationale: Ordinary matrix powers preserve the eigenbasis of a symmetric input, so this is exactly a scalar question on [0,1]. The scalar endpoints are fixed. For 0<x<1 let u=x² and a=1+h(1-u)>1. Substitution gives 2z_h(x)(1-u)/x=1+a²-u(1+a+a⁴-a³). The denominator minus the numerator in the resulting zero formula for u is a(a-1)²(a+1)>0, so the parametrization is reversible and covers all interior zeros at positive h. The crossing function is G(a)=a-1+(a²+1)/(a(a²-1)). Its derivative has the sign of a⁴-4a²+1 on a>1, so it has one minimum at sqrt(2+sqrt(3)). There a-1/a=sqrt(2) and (a²+1)/(a²-1)=sqrt(3), yielding G(a)=2sqrt(2)-1. Continuity from h=0 gives positivity below the first crossing and nonnegativity at it; uniqueness of the minimizing a yields the sole interior zero at equality. At fixed u the quartic coefficients in descending h have signs -,-,ambiguous,+,+, with any zero coefficient omitted. Descartes' rule and the negative leading coefficient give one positive root, with strict negativity thereafter. Applying it at the critical input proves the same witness for every h above the frontier. Independently y>=0 and y-1=(1-x)(hx(1+x)-1); the supremum of x(1+x) as x approaches 1 from below is 2, giving the universal source threshold 1/2 including equality. These arguments address all matrix dimensions without a numerical search.
